name: yoast
notes: wpseo_titles/wpseo_social captured authored: real site-admin config (title/meta-description templates, social defaults, breadcrumb/company settings). KNOWN GAP, narrower than before task #11 wave 2: both blobs can embed an attachment id for a logo/default-social-image sub-key (e.g. company_logo_id/person_logo_id/og_default_image_id) that is NOT yet declared here — the json_refs mechanism that WOULD close this now exists and is proven elsewhere in this manifest (wpseo_taxonomy_meta below) and in manifests/elementor.json, but applying it to wpseo_titles/wpseo_social's own specific sub-keys was out of this wave's scope (task #11 wave 2 was scoped to wpseo_taxonomy_meta for the options side) and their exact shapes were not empirically verified this session — adding json_refs paths here without checking real bytes first would be exactly the kind of guess this project's discipline exists to avoid. `wp duo lint`'s bare_id class (now also depth-aware for any structured value, but wpseo_titles/wpseo_social are captured as plain whole-value strings here, not json_refs-declared, so the SHALLOW scan is what would apply) would still flag such an id if it's a top-level scalar; it would not see one nested inside these blobs without a json_refs declaration to trigger the deep scan. Not exercised by this manifest's conformance seed (no logo/social image configured there). Next step for whoever picks this up: seed a logo id, read the real bytes, then add json_refs the same way this file's wpseo_taxonomy_meta entry does.

wpseo (the main options blob) deliberately NOT captured: mixes genuine feature toggles with env-local bookkeeping (first_activated_on timestamp, dismissed-notice UI state, and the version key Yoast uses to gate its own upgrade routines). Capturing it wholesale would let a stale captured version silently roll back another environment's upgrade-routine gate. v0's options model has no sub-key split to capture only the safe half.

wpseo_taxonomy_meta now captured authored (task #11 wave 2 closed this gap): PHP-serialized `{taxonomy_name: {term_id: {...fields...}}}` (verified empirically via WPSEO_Taxonomy_Meta::set_values(), Yoast's own documented public API — not guessed; term_id keys are genuinely PHP int-typed, e.g. `i:13;`, not strings). key_refs (`{"path": "$.*", "kind": "term"}`) rewrites the per-taxonomy submap's term-id KEYS through the ledger; json_refs rewrites the two id-VALUED sibling fields the same $defaults_per_term array declares (wpseo_opengraph-image-id / wpseo_twitter-image-id, both stored as digit STRINGS — `s:2:"11"` — hence cast:"string" on both paths, preserving the exact serialized type on apply). Every other field (wpseo_desc, wpseo_noindex, the plain-URL wpseo_opengraph-image/wpseo_twitter-image siblings, ...) is tokenize_text()'d automatically by the same whole-structure string-leaf pass json_refs/key_refs values always get — no path needed for those. Round-trips proven end-to-end (fx1/fx2, genuine term-id and attachment-id divergence, raw DB byte inspection both sides) and lint-clean both directions (declared paths clean; an undeclared image-id path, tested by deliberately dropping it, is precisely flagged and doesn't false-positive on the correctly-token-keyed term entry it lives inside).

wpseo_rss/wpseo_internallinks/wpseo_xml look like safe, config-heavy candidates for a future pass; left undeclared (uncaptured, never blocking) here rather than classified from memory without empirical verification against a running install.

rebuilder verified against a running install: 'wp yoast index' takes its OWN --skip-confirmation flag for non-interactive use, not the generic wp-cli --yes (confirmed empirically — --yes is rejected as an unknown parameter). Separately, and unrelated to that flag: since Yoast SEO 15.1, indexable creation is production-only by design (gated on wp_get_environment_type() === 'production', bypassable only via the Yoast\WP\SEO\should_index_indexables filter) — every sandbox/CI env here runs WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=local, so this rebuilder is expected to warn-not-fail (Apply's rebuild pass treats rebuilder exit != 0 as a warning) in every environment this repo's tests ever run against, and will only actually index on a real production site. Not a bug; do not silence the warning by defining the override filter in the agent — that would change Yoast's own behavior underneath every site, production included, which is Yoast's call to make per-site, not Duo's to make globally.
